newsitem.title: USA: Hugoton sets 1997 spending at $75 million.
newsitem.headline: Hugoton sets 1997 spending at $75 million.

text.p: Hugoton Energy Corp said Wednesday it will spend a record $75 million on capital improvements in 1997, up from the $40 million actually spent in 1996.
The budget allocates $50.6 million for drilling, $5.1 million for associated seismic costs and $4.3 million in land and miscellaneous expenditures.
The budget also allows for $15 million of small, strategic acquisitions, the company said in a statement.

The company said it plans to fund the 1997 drilling budget with internally generated cash. The remainder of its planned capital expenditures, along with any major acquisitions, will be funded by borrowings under the company's $250 million unsecured bank credit facility.

Hugoton said it drilled a total of 66 wells during 1996 and completed 56 of them, for a success rate of 85 percent. The company accelerated its drilling program during the second half of 1996 and drilled 65 percent of its wells during the last half of the year.

Geographically, the 1997 drilling budget will be expended 30 percent in southwestern Kansas and the mid-continent area, 30 percent in the Spraberry Trend of West Texas, 20 percent in the Austin Chalk Trend located in Texas and Louisiana, and 20 percent in the Williston Basin of North Dakota.
About 60 percent of the drilling budget will be spent on development drilling and the remaining 40 percent on exploration projects.
Hugoton is an independent oil and natural gas development and production company.
